traits.notes: The seedling exhibits a distinct whorled leaf arrangement at the apex with prominent secondary venation and a coarse, toothed margin.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves are clearly seen radiating from a single node in the apical cluster)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are gathered closely together at the apex of the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves consist of a single blade)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): toothed (margin displays distinct, coarse, irregular teeth)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaf is widest at the middle and tapers towards both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (leaf tapers to a distinct, elongated point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base appears broadly rounded to slightly cordate)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): highly visible, prominent, and regularly spaced (strongly impressed on the upper surface)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface reflects light and appears glossy)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): present (fine, short hairs are visible on the lighter-colored new growth and along the veins)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are distinct but relatively short compared to the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the main stem appears hard and brownish)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the visible stem surface appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: brown (visible sections of the stem are dark brown)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stem surface appears relatively uniform without ridges)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): present (dried, brown stipules are visible at the base of the petioles in the apical cluster)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a distinct whorled leaf arrangement at the apex with prominent secondary venation and a coarse, toothed margin.
